title: Excessive object allocation in hot paths
summary: Allocating short-lived hashes, arrays, strings, or objects in tight loops increases GC pressure.
rationale: Ruby performance is often dominated by allocation behavior rather than raw instruction count. Avoidable temporary objects can degrade throughput.

impact.notes: Impact increases in hot paths, large collections, high-traffic Rails actions, background jobs, or repeated request paths.

remediation.guidance: Reuse immutable constants, reduce temporary object creation, prefer streaming transformations, and profile before micro-optimizing.
remediation.tradeoffs: May require refactoring for readability, query shape, or framework conventions.
